Commentary.Commentary: We are back for West Indies' reply. The South African players make their way out on the field. Followed by Kyle Mayers and Brandon King who walk out to open for West Indies. Bjorn Fortuin will start with the new ball.
... The Run Chase ...

Sheldon Cottrell was the pick of the Windies bowlers with 2 wickets for 31 runs in his three overs of which he was peppered for 24 in his last over.  The rest of the bowlers supported him well and kept the run rate in check, although they might feel they lost their advantage as they head into the break. Right then, the target now for West Indies is 132. Can they do it and take a 1-0 lead in this series? We shall find out together. The second essay coming up shortly. Stay tuned.

A 13-ball 47 runs partnership between David Miller and Sisanda Magala has got South Africa to 131 for 8 in their allotted 11 overs. Having put into bat first, South Africa lost de Kock early for a golden duck. The other batters kept swinging their bat and kept the run rate going around 10 per over.  West Indies picked up wickets regularly and half of the Proteas side was back in the hut inside 40 balls. Reeza Hendricks played a handy knock while Aiden Markram and Rilee Rossouw chipped in with small contributions. David Miller was again the savior as he made a brilliant 48(22) and took his side into a comfortable position after being in some trouble early on.
Swing and a miss! Short one, outside off. Anrich Nortje slashes hard but misses. South Africa end the innings at 131/8.

Commentary.Commentary: Anrich Nortje is the new batter in.

Commentary.Commentary: Right then, the prolonged wait comes to an end. The two umpires are seen making their way out on the field. The West Indies players are seen to be in a huddle before they spread out on the field. Followed by Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks who walk out to open for South Africa. It will be Akeal Hosein to start with the new ball. A huge dark lurking around the ground. Hopefully, the rain gods do not interrupt once again. Here we go...

Aiden Markram, the skipper of South Africa is in for a chat. He says that they would've bowled first as well but they will try to put a sufficent total on the board. Mentions it is about encouraging guys about expressing themselves in the shortest format. Adds that it is a fresh start from them.

Rovman Powell, the captain of West Indies says that they will bowl first as it’s the trend on the venue. Adds they will have to do the right things and play good cricket. Mentions that he will have to lead from the front and the team will follow. Says that they are going with a balanced side.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (WK), Reeza Hendricks, Rilee Rossouw, Aiden Markram (C), Heinrich Klaasen, David Miller, Wayne Parnell, Sisanda Magala, Bjorn Fortuin, Anrich Nortje and Tabraiz Shamsi.

West Indies, who are known for their lethal approach in the shortest format, find themselves in a transition phase, and have decided to hand the captaincy to Rovam Powell, he has captained once before in a T20I match. To be honest, there is no shortage of power-hitters in this batting rank and if they explode, it will be a challenge to stop them. Two strong teams colliding, only makes this match more enticing. Who will get over the line? We shall find out soon, as the toss isn't far away.

Hello and a warm welcome to all. It is now time for the first T20I match between South Africa and West Indies. This is the start of the final leg of this multi-format series. It will be Aiden Markram who will lead this Proteas side. South Africa are a solid unit with experience across all departments. They will hope that they can get things started on a positive note under the new leadership.
... MATCH DAY ...

Following a closely fought ODI series in which both teams shared the trophy, it is now time for action in the game's shortest format. South Africa and West Indies will now face off in a three-match T20I series. The first two T20Is of the series will be played at the SuperSport Park in Centurion before the caravan shifts to the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg for the third and final T20I of the series. The change in format has brought about a change in leadership for the hosts, with Aiden Markram taking over from Temba Bavuma for the T20I series. Aiden Markram, along with Quinton de Kock, Heinrich Klaasen, and Rilee Rossouw, will be crucial to the chances of the hosts with the bat. South Africa have a lethal pace attack with Kagiso Rabada, Anrich Nortje, and Lungi Ngidi in their ranks. The spin duo of Bjorn Fortuin and Tabraiz Shamsi did a decent job in the ODI series and will be expected to do even better in the T20I series. West Indies, on the other hand, will play the T20I series under the leadership of Rovman Powell. In the batting department, the onus will be on Johnson Charles, Kyle Mayers, and Nicholas Pooran in this series. The seam bowling duties for the visitors will rest on the shoulders of Alzarri Joseph, Sheldon Cottrell, and Jason Holder. In the spin department, Akeal Hosein and Yannic Cariah will hold the key for West Indies. In the previous five T20I meetings between the two sides, South Africa have come out on top on four occasions, and as a result, they hold the upper hand heading into this series. Will South Africa continue their dominance over West Indies in the T20I format? Or will we see West Indies spring a surprise? We shall find out soon enough.
